disease_label_per_paper: Clostridioides difficile infection leading to fulminant colitis with toxic megacolon
presentation_summary: 23-year-old male nursing home resident with remote anoxic brain injury was hospitalized with fever, cough, and green sputum after three days of linezolid plus piperacillin-tazobactam.
Immediately before admission he developed abdominal distension, diarrhea, and vomiting.
Admission vitals showed temperature 39.6 C, respiratory rate 34/min, pulse 126/min; WBC was 19.65 with 90% neutrophils.
Abdomen was mildly distended and nontender; CT showed marked ascending-colon wall thickening and dilated bowel loops measuring up to 11 cm in the cecum/ascending colon.
He underwent total colectomy; the colon was dilated to 11 cm with edematous mucosa and yellow pseudomembranes. Stool qualitative PCR detected C. difficile toxin B gene.
